name: Bon Iver
label: 4AD
lede: Justin Vernon went to his father's hunting cabin to get over a band, a breakup and a sick liver, came back with nine songs he called demos, and ended up on Kanye West records, Taylor Swift records and the Grammy stage.

hero.by: Bon Iver in Stockholm, 2011. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Good winter
eras.text: A band split, a relationship ended and mononucleosis hit Justin Vernon's liver, all in 2006. He drove home to Wisconsin and spent the winter in a cabin with a microphone, a guitar and a Northern Exposure box set.

years.cap: DeYarmond Edison: Justin Vernon, Joe Westerlund, Phil Cook and Brad Cook
years.src: New Yorker: Into the Woods · Wikipedia: Bon Iver
years.h: DeYarmond Edison breaks up in Raleigh
years.p: Vernon's Eau Claire friends' band, relocated to North Carolina, falls apart. He splits with his girlfriend and gets mononucleosis that hits his liver.
years.xp: Months earlier, in March 2006, Vernon had made a solo EP, Hazelton, singing two songs almost entirely in falsetto and stacking his own voice into a chorus. The New Yorker's Sasha Frere-Jones heard the whole Bon Iver sound starting there.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Into the Woods
years.h: An episode of Northern Exposure supplies the name
years.p: Bedridden, Vernon watches the 1990s show on DVD. Alaskans greet the first snow with "bon hiver," good winter. He drops the h because hiver reminded him of liver.

years.cap: Justin Vernon in a For Emma press photo
q: I knew that I wanted to be where it was cold.
years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Into the Woods
years.h: Vernon moves into his father's hunting cabin for the winter
years.p: Three months in Dunn County, western Wisconsin, with a Shure SM57, an old Silvertone guitar and his brother's drums. He plays everything.
years.xp:
He hadn't planned to make a record. "I knew that I wanted to be alone and I knew that I wanted to be where it was cold," he told Exclaim!.

He wrote by recording wordless melodies, then listening back until syllables became words. Frere-Jones heard "Flume" as the song that brought Vernon home and pushed him into writing for the falsetto.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Into the Woods
years.h: 500 CDs in card sleeves, and 17 go to the press
years.p: Vernon self-releases For Emma, Forever Ago with two shows at the House of Rock in Eau Claire, one all-ages, one 21-plus.
years.xp:
The songs were meant as demos for labels, maybe to be re-recorded; friends talked him into releasing them as they were. Manager Kyle Frenette told HitQuarters that after My Old Kentucky Blog wrote it up in June, "it snowballed."

Emma isn't the girlfriend from Raleigh. Frere-Jones reported it's a stand-in name for a woman Vernon dated years earlier in Eau Claire.

years.h: Sean Carey tells Vernon he can already play every song
years.p: Carey walks up at one of the first shows and says so; he becomes the drummer. Vernon met Matthew McCaughan on tour with The Rosebuds in May.

years.h: A Pitchfork rave, a CMJ set, then Jagjaguwar
years.p: After the October review and a CMJ showcase, majors and indies call. Frenette says they picked Jagjaguwar because its ideals matched theirs.

eras.title: The cabin goes worldwide
eras.text: Jagjaguwar put the record out in America and 4AD took it to Britain and Europe. Within a year the songs were on Letterman, on network TV dramas and in a Kanye West sample.

years.cap: Bon Iver at the Black Cat, Washington DC, 2008
years.h: Jagjaguwar reissues For Emma and sends Bon Iver out with Black Mountain
years.p: The official release and a joint tour start the same night.

yt: "Skinny Love" on Later... with Jools Holland, 2008
years.h: 4AD releases For Emma in the UK and Europe
years.p: Mojo and Uncut both give it five stars and make it album of the month. "Skinny Love" is iTunes UK's free single of the week.

years.h: Vernon's old guitar student is now in the band
years.p: At the Bowery Ballroom, Mike Noyce, a former guitar student who left college to tour, plays beside Carey on drums. Vernon sits boxed in by his amps and pedals.

years.h: The Vernon brothers buy a veterinary clinic in Fall Creek
years.p: They turn it into April Base studio, built over the clinic's old swimming pool, three miles from the house Vernon grew up in.
years.xp: Vernon: "It's also only three miles from the house I grew up in, and just ten minutes from the bar where my parents met."

years.src: New Yorker: Into the Woods · Wikipedia: Bon Iver
years.h: A heckler at Town Hall, and the whole room sings "The Wolves"
years.p: A man yells about layoffs and the economy before the encore. Vernon answers that it "seemed really heartfelt," then leads the crowd through the song's five sung words.
years.xp:
Vernon asked crowds to sing along at every show; he'd told Pitchfork the songs needed "80–500 people singing." The New Yorker's Sasha Frere-Jones stayed in his seat after the room emptied.

On December 11 the band played "Skinny Love" on the Late Show with David Letterman.

years.h: The Blood Bank EP follows the cabin record
years.p: The EP lands as "Skinny Love" hits 21 on Triple J's Hottest 100 for 2008.

years.h: From the cabin to Lollapalooza and the Twilight soundtrack
years.p: A Lollapalooza set, "Roslyn" with [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] for New Moon, and "Brackett, WI" on Dark Was the Night. In October, the cover of The Fader.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Bon Iver Is Searching
years.h: Kanye West builds "Lost in the World" on "Woods"
years.p: Vernon also sings on "Monster" and "Dark Fantasy" on My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy. He plays SXSW with GOOD Music the next March.

eras.title: A band now, and a Grammy
eras.text: The second album was built in the old vet clinic with pedal steel, bass saxophone and horns, and the touring band doubled. It won two Grammys, and then Vernon shut it down.

years.h: iTunes sells the new album a month early, by accident
years.p: Apple pulls it, but not before a handful of buyers download it. The lyrics go up on the album's site.

years.h: Every song a place: Bon Iver, Bon Iver
years.p: Jagjaguwar and 4AD release it, with [[Colin Stetson|22b2f6dc-fcc2-490d-a462-f972a692ce12]] on bass sax, Greg Leisz on pedal steel and Gregory Euclide's painting on the cover.
years.xp:
"I brought in a lot of people to change my voice, not my singing voice, but my role as the author of this band," Vernon told Rolling Stone.

Critics split. Paste gave it nine out of ten. AllMusic's Tim Sendra called it "sub-Enya with a beard." In December, Pitchfork named it the album of 2011.

years.h: "Holocene" gets a video from director Nabil
years.p: The second album's centrepiece gets Record and Song of the Year nominations in November.

years.big: "It's not that the Grammys are evil, they've just been around the longest"
q: It's not that the Grammys are evil, they've just been around the longest.
years.h: Best New Artist, five years after the cabin
years.p: Bon Iver wins Best New Artist and Best Alternative Music Album, over [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] among others. Vernon tells the room he's uncomfortable up there.
years.xp:
A few days later Vernon told Spin the Grammys felt self-important, though he'd enjoyed the night. Grizzly Bear's Ed Droste had sent him a note: "Hey man, go win one for the indies."

Eight days before, the band had played "Holocene" and "Beth/Rest" on Saturday Night Live.

years.cap: Bon Iver at New Orleans Jazz Fest, April 2012
years.h: In Dublin, Vernon calls it the last show "at least for a while"
years.p: Jagjaguwar says the band is just going off cycle after two busy years. They don't play again for almost three.

eras.title: Glitches, saxophones and a festival at home
eras.text: The comeback came at a festival Vernon co-founded in Eau Claire, and the music had gone strange: chopped voices, numbers for titles, a saxophone group called Sad Sax of Shit.

years.h: "Heavenly Father" for Zach Braff's Wish I Was Here
years.p: The first new Bon Iver song since the break, on a film soundtrack.

years.cap: Justin Vernon at the first Eaux Claires festival, Eau Claire, Wisconsin, July 2015
years.h: First show in nearly three years, at Eaux Claires
years.p: At the Eau Claire festival the band debuts "666 ʇ" and "89". Only the first makes the next album; "89" becomes a fan favorite anyway.

years.cap: The Staves with Bon Iver, Wilton's Music Hall
years.h: The Staves sing inside Bon Iver on a tour of Asia
years.p: The first tour since 2012 adds Andrew Fitzpatrick and The Staves, whose album Vernon produced.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Bon Iver Is Searching
years.h: 22, A Million and song titles in symbols
years.p: Pitchfork compares it to Kid A. A 22-second Facebook stream started the rollout in July.
years.xp:
The record leans on processed voices and a saxophone group called Sad Sax of Shit. Pitchfork heard "deeply felt songs about uncertainty" behind the glitches.

Talking to the New Yorker in 2024, Vernon picked one of its made-up words, "fuckified," as something "you just have to kind of let it out."

years.h: Autumn: twelve minutes on taking the band into arenas
years.p: A short film about keeping arena shows intimate, with motion-tracked lights and 3D sound.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Bon Iver Is Searching
years.h: Recorded in Texas, posted one song an hour
years.p: On August 8 the band posts the album track by track, three weeks early. It's nominated for Album of the Year.
years.xp: April Base was being renovated, so the band set up at Sonic Ranch in Texas for about two months. Vernon later said he heard the four albums as the four seasons, with i,i as autumn.

years.cap: Bon Iver on the i,i tour, October 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Bon Iver Is Searching
years.h: Jenn Wasner joins for the i,i arena tour
years.p: [[Wye Oak|3c8ff4c9-b5b9-4e78-ad9d-5157c323de24]]'s Jenn Wasner, who sings on i,i, makes the touring band a six-piece.
years.xp: Vernon's proudest arena moment, he told the New Yorker, was at Barclays Center with [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]] opening: Sean Carey and Michael Lewis "throttling free jazz to an arena that is absolutely understanding what we're doing."

eras.title: Exile, then a sable
eras.text: A Taylor Swift duet gave Bon Iver its first top-ten single. Then Vernon stepped off the road, rebuilt, and came back with his own voice nearly alone.

years.h: "PDLIF" sends every cent to COVID relief
years.p: "Please Don't Live In Fear" goes out for Direct Relief. Kendrick Lamar and Baby Keem later sample it on "The Hillbillies".

years.src: Wikipedia: Bon Iver · New Yorker: Bon Iver Is Searching
years.h: "Exile" with Taylor Swift reaches the Billboard top ten
years.p: Bon Iver's first top-ten hit. The pair don't meet in person until long after folklore is out.
years.xp: "I wasn't starstruck," Vernon told the New Yorker. "You're somebody that I would have been very close friends with in high school." Bon Iver is on evermore's title track in December too.

years.src: New Yorker: Bon Iver Is Searching
years.h: Vernon breaks down mid-song in Duluth
years.p: Playing "[715] CRΣΣKS" alone before six or seven thousand people near the end of the last run, he starts to weep while the crowd cheers.
years.xp: "I was getting ready to start saying goodbye to the last sixteen years, in a way," he told Amanda Petrusich. "That whole night in, night out, let's excavate Justin. I'm not built for it."

years.cap: Justin Vernon in a press photo for SABLE, fABLE
years.src: New Yorker: Bon Iver Is Searching · Wikipedia: Bon Iver
yt: "S P E Y S I D E" (official video)
years.h: Vernon strips back to one voice on the SABLE, EP
years.p: Written partly in Key West in early 2021, recorded at April Base, with Greg Leisz on pedal steel again. Erinn Springer shoots black-and-white videos with Vernon's face in them.
years.xp:
Vernon called it "a triptych" running "from accepting anxiety to accepting guilt to accepting hope." Speyside is a whisky region; he didn't want to call the song "Key West."

The title, he said, was him asking whether he'd been "repeating a cycle of sorrow."
play: S P E Y S I D E

years.h: SABLE, fABLE: the EP becomes the prologue
years.p: The three SABLE, songs open a full album billed as "an outstretched hand." It's nominated for Best Alternative Music Album.

years.h: Volumes opens the live vault
years.p: An archival series starts with live recordings by the six-piece from 2019 to 2023, out April 3 on Jagjaguwar.
